discovery: Experimental discovery of the Higgs boson by the ATLAS and CMS experiments at the LHC
motivation: The 2013 Prize honored the prediction of the Brout-Englert-Higgs mechanism, but the experimental discovery that confirmed it has not been recognized. In 2012 the ATLAS and CMS experiments observed a new scalar boson near 125 GeV. Its measured couplings, spin and parity have since established it as the Higgs boson of the Standard Model. Peter Jenni co-founded ATLAS and led it as spokesperson through its design and construction. Tejinder Virdee co-founded CMS and was central to its electromagnetic calorimeter, which was essential to the diphoton discovery channel. Fabiola Gianotti led ATLAS at the time of discovery and drove the analysis strategy. Together they designed the detectors, trigger systems and data pipelines that made it possible to find a rare signal in billions of collisions per second. This was a qualitative leap in experimental capability, and it opened the direct experimental study of electroweak symmetry breaking.
